how: 25 of the 100, stratified: 15 with structured data and 10 without, 9 with 3 or more font families, 4 with a broken og:image, 2 where the first font pass found no text. For each: the raw HTML head and JSON-LD read by hand, a full-page screenshot looked at, an exhaustive font census (Chromium's own record of the font file that drew every visible text element, CSS.getPlatformFontsForNode), and robots.txt, the sitemap, og:image and favicon.ico requested again with curl.

truthNotes.fonts: Truth = distinct typefaces a Windows or Mac visitor sees for at least 2% of the page's text, judged from the census, the CSS stacks and the screenshot. A named Windows/Mac font (Verdana, Tahoma) counts as its own family even though the Linux measuring machine substitutes it.
truthNotes.ogImage: Truth = the image works as a link-preview image: it loads and is a format the big previewers accept (not SVG).
